materials.name: concrete
materials.description: A composite construction material composed of fine and coarse aggregate bonded together with a fluid cement (cement paste) that hardens over time.

carbon.description: Embodied carbon for typical general purpose concrete.

compressive.description: Characteristic compressive strength for C25/30 concrete.

elastic.description: Secant modulus of elasticity for C25/30 concrete.

recyclability.description: Fraction of concrete that can be recycled into aggregate.

tensile.description: Mean axial tensile strength for C25/30 concrete.

materials.name: cement
materials.description: A fine, grey powder, typically Portland cement, that acts as a hydraulic binder when mixed with water, forming a paste that hardens to bind aggregates in concrete and mortar.

density.description: Typical bulk density of loose Portland cement powder.

carbon.description: Embodied carbon for Ordinary Portland Cement (OPC).

thermalConductivity.description: Thermal conductivity of hardened cement paste.

materials.name: sand
materials.description: A granular material composed of finely divided rock and mineral particles, typically silica. Used as an aggregate in concrete, mortar, and asphalt, and for various landscaping and construction purposes.

density.description: Typical density for dry, loose sand.

carbon.description: Embodied carbon for aggregates (sand and gravel).

recyclability.description: Sand and gravel are highly reusable as aggregates.

materials.name: gravel
materials.description: A loose aggregation of rock fragments, typically used as an aggregate in construction, for drainage, or as a decorative landscaping material.

carbon.description: Embodied carbon from extraction, crushing, and transport.

compressive.description: Compressive strength of individual rock particles (e.g., limestone, granite) that constitute gravel.

elastic.description: Elastic modulus of individual rock particles.

recyclability.description: High potential for reuse and recycling as aggregate.

materials.name: stone
materials.description: A natural, hard, non-metallic mineral matter, typically quarried and used for structural elements, cladding, paving, and decorative purposes.

materials.name: mortar
materials.description: A workable paste used to bind building blocks such as bricks, stones, or concrete masonry units together, fill and seal the irregular gaps between them, and sometimes add decorative colors or patterns to masonry walls.

materials.name: grout
materials.description: A cementitious mixture used to fill gaps, reinforce masonry, or bond building components. It typically consists of cement, sand, water, and sometimes admixtures.

carbon.description: Embodied carbon for typical cementitious grout.

compressive.description: Typical compressive strength for a general-purpose structural grout.

elastic.description: Typical elastic modulus for cementitious grout.

recyclability.description: Recyclability of hardened cementitious grout as aggregate.

tensile.description: Typical tensile strength (flexural) for cementitious grout.

thermalConductivity.description: Typical thermal conductivity for cementitious grout.

materials.name: steel
materials.description: A strong, versatile alloy of iron and carbon, widely used in construction for structural frames, reinforcement, and various components due to its high strength-to-weight ratio and ductility.

materials.name: rebar
materials.description: Reinforcing bar, typically made from carbon steel, used to strengthen concrete structures.

materials.name: aluminum
materials.description: A lightweight, ductile, and corrosion-resistant metal widely used in construction, aerospace, and packaging.

materials.name: copper
materials.description: A reddish-orange metallic element, highly ductile and malleable, with excellent electrical and thermal conductivity. Commonly used in electrical wiring, plumbing, roofing, and various alloys.

materials.name: iron
materials.description: A common ferrous metal, often used in construction as cast iron for pipes, fittings, and decorative elements. Known for its high compressive strength and good castability.

materials.name: lead
materials.description: A heavy, soft, malleable, and ductile metal. It is known for its high density, low melting point, and excellent corrosion resistance. Commonly used in batteries, radiation shielding, and as an alloying element.

carbon.description: Embodied carbon for primary lead production.

compressive.description: Typical yield strength, as lead is very ductile.

materials.name: zinc
materials.description: A bluish-white, lustrous, diamagnetic metal. Zinc is the fourth most common metal in terms of production, after iron, aluminum, and copper. It is used for galvanizing steel, in alloys like brass, and in batteries.

materials.name: wire
materials.description: A slender, flexible strand of metal, typically made from steel, used in various applications from structural reinforcement to electrical conduction.

materials.name: bricks
materials.description: Traditional building units made from fired clay, used for walls, paving, and other construction elements. Known for durability and thermal mass.

materials.name: blocks
materials.description: Standard concrete masonry units (CMU), commonly known as concrete blocks, used for load-bearing and non-load-bearing walls.

materials.name: granite
materials.description: A common intrusive felsic igneous rock, typically light-colored with visible grains, used widely in construction for its durability and aesthetic appeal.

materials.name: marble
materials.description: A metamorphic rock composed primarily of recrystallized carbonate minerals, most commonly calcite or dolomite. It is widely used for sculpture and as a building material.

materials.name: limestone
materials.description: A common sedimentary rock, primarily composed of calcium carbonate, often used in construction for cladding, flooring, and as aggregate.

recyclability.description: High potential for reuse as crushed aggregate.

materials.name: sandstone
materials.description: A common sedimentary rock composed mainly of sand-sized mineral grains or rock fragments. Often used in construction for cladding, paving, and structural elements.

materials.name: slate
materials.description: A fine-grained, foliated, homogeneous metamorphic rock derived from an original shale-type sedimentary rock, commonly used for roofing, flooring, and cladding.

materials.name: glass
materials.description: A hard, brittle, transparent or translucent amorphous solid, typically made by fusing sand with soda and lime. Commonly used in windows, doors, and facades.

materials.name: terracotta
materials.description: A type of fired clay, typically brownish-red in color, used for roofing tiles, floor tiles, pipes, and decorative architectural elements. It is porous unless glazed.

materials.name: softwood
materials.description: General classification for wood from coniferous trees, typically lighter in color and less dense than hardwoods. Commonly used for structural framing, joinery, and pulp.

density.description: Typical density for common softwoods like pine or spruce at 12% moisture content.

carbon.description: Embodied carbon for sawn softwood, including processing.

compressive.description: Compressive strength parallel to grain for typical softwood.

elastic.description: Modulus of elasticity parallel to grain for typical softwood.

recyclability.description: Fraction of softwood that can be recycled or reused.

tensile.description: Tensile strength parallel to grain for typical softwood.

materials.name: hardwood
materials.description: General deciduous timber (e.g. oak, beech).

materials.name: douglas
materials.description: A strong, durable softwood commonly used for structural timber.

materials.name: plywood
materials.description: A sheet material made from layers of wood veneer glued together.

density.description: Density is a measure of how tightly packed the mass is inside an object

materials.name: osb
materials.description: Engineered board of compressed, glued wood strands.

materials.name: glulam
materials.description: Structural timber of glued laminations.

materials.name: clt
materials.description: Panels of crosswise-glued timber layers.

materials.name: bamboo
materials.description: Fast-growing grass used as a strong, light building material.

materials.name: pvc
materials.description: Common rigid/flexible thermoplastic.

materials.name: hdpe
materials.description: Tough thermoplastic used for pipes and sheets.

materials.name: eps
materials.description: Rigid closed-cell foam insulation.

materials.name: xps
materials.description: Rigid extruded foam insulation, higher moisture resistance than EPS.

materials.name: mineralwool
materials.description: Fibrous insulation from spun mineral fibres.

materials.name: sprayfoam
materials.description: Polyurethane spray foam insulation, typically closed-cell, used for thermal insulation and air sealing in building envelopes. It expands upon application to fill cavities and gaps.

density.description: Typical density for closed-cell spray foam.

compressive.description: Typical compressive strength for closed-cell SPF (approx. 2 lb/ft3 density).

recyclability.description: Limited recyclability for post-consumer waste, often downcycled or incinerated.

thermalConductivity.description: Typical thermal conductivity for closed-cell spray foam.

materials.name: drywall
materials.description: A common interior wall and ceiling finish material made from gypsum plaster pressed between two sheets of thick paper.
